newsitem.title: UK: Investec completes UK stockbroker buy.
newsitem.headline: Investec completes UK stockbroker buy.

text.p: South Africa's Investec Bank Ltd completed the purchase of British investment manager and stockbroker Carr Sheppards from Banque Indosuez on Friday, Carr Sheppards' chief executive told Reuters on Monday.
"They completed (the deal) at about 1430 GMT on Friday," Fred Carr said, adding that neither party was keen to comment on the content of the deal or the amount paid.
Earlier London's Evening Standard newspaper said Investec had paid around 20 million stg for Carr Sheppards, which has more than 2.5 billion stg in funds under management or advice.
Carr said he could not comment on the sum paid but acknowledged that key members of staff would be locked in to the firm following the sale.
"All the senior people have got tie-ins of one sort or another," he said, adding that these were the normal sort of agreements signed by those working in the business.
Carr said jobs were not likely to be cut. The firm employs more than 200 staff in London, Farnham and Reigate in the south of England.
Investec already has substantial international operations and owns London-based Allied Trust Bank and Clive Discount Co.

A strategic review by Banque Indosuez in 1995 concluded that Carr Sheppards was a non-core business and the firm was put up for sale. Investec said it was in advanced talks to buy the company in October and said it hoped to seal the deal by the end of 1996.
